issues.description: signing_mode_enum's four-way truth table relies on an unstated fall-through default.
issues.detail: Three explicit elif branches followed by a bare 'return CHIP_0002' force the reader to enumerate (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations to verify correctness. Rewrite as an exhaustive match or a dict keyed by the (is_hex, safe_mode) tuple so the fourth case is spelled out rather than implicit.

issues.description: SigningMode-to-bytes dispatch is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature.
issues.detail: The same mode-to-message-bytes mapping ladder appears in both functions in signing.py. Extract a single private helper _message_to_bytes(mode, message) -> bytes so the encoding table lives once. Otherwise adding a new CHIP mode requires updating two parallel ladders that can silently drift.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum exists as both a module function and as @property wrappers — pick one.
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a free signing_mode_enum(request) and also adds @property signing_mode_enum on SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID that just delegate to it. Two names resolving to one behavior forces future maintainers to grep both. Collapse to a single shared helper or a mixin.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring still references a 'request' parameter that no longer exists.
issues.detail: The function now takes (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address) but the docstring reads ':param request:'. Stale documentation that misrepresents the signature is worse than none. Either describe the actual parameters or delete the stub.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method that uses no instance state.
issues.detail: Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic only calls calculate_synthetic_secret_key with a module-level constant and never reads self. Binding it as a method adds nothing. Move it to signing.py as a module-level function (or a staticmethod) so the shape matches what the code actually does.

issues.description: sign_message and verify_signature disagree on how to handle unknown SigningMode values.
issues.detail: sign_message silently treats any unenumerated mode as CHIP_0002 via an else branch, while verify_signature raises on unsupported modes. Two functions sharing one enum should share one discipline — either both exhaustive-match or both refuse the unknown. Asymmetric handling invites future drift.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a sound mechanical extraction: three near-duplicate sign_message implementations across Wallet/DIDWallet/NFTWallet collapse into one signing utility, which is the right direction. The criticism is uniform: the extraction stops one step short of cleanup. The (is_hex, safe_mode) -> SigningMode truth table relies on an implicit fall-through default; the mode-to-bytes mapping is still duplicated inside signing.py; and signing_mode_enum lives as both a free function and properties. Smaller drift includes a stale 'request' docstring and an instance method that uses no instance state. Needs-work, all fixes cheap, then land it.
